OPERATION OPEN DOOR
Syria / fictional village hostage rescue / single-player OH-58D flight of four

SITUATION
Six hostages are held in the identified village building. Satellite intelligence precisely locates the building and a Strela-10 launcher. These are fixed intelligence points, not live tracking. Other guards and reinforcements are hidden. Labels are OFF and F10 units are friendly-only. No fighter aircraft or other air support is available.

FLIGHT
Anvil 1-1: you. All four Kiowas start hot ON THE GROUND at four separate, visible native DCS helipads in FARP FOOTHOLD, 60 m apart. Native hot-ground starts use zero terrain-relative altitude; no copied barometric spawn height. Lifeline has its own fifth pad. Set your physical collective fully down before Fly. Fuel tanker/depot, ammunition trucks/canopy, ground crew, command post and repair tent are present from mission start, with unlimited warehouse resources. Use Ground Crew while parked; shut down for repairs. Lead and #2 each carry two Hellfires and a .50-cal gun with 500 rounds. #3/#4 each carry the gun plus seven M151 rockets. Fuel: 400 lb (181.4 kg) each (within the checked 333.69 kg capacity; hover/gross weight and endurance need cockpit verification). Lead PDU enabled. Use normal wingman radio commands. Monitor fuel and preserve a reserve; fuel-capacity compliance is not an endurance guarantee.
Native trees-only scenery zones clear all five departure pads, the service areas and an initial 600 m lane toward the IP at mission start. Buildings and terrain are retained. Tree clearance and ground fit still need visual confirmation in DCS.
Lifeline is one built-in AI UH-60A Black Hawk on its own nearby pad. It starts following you when you lift off and holds back as you approach the village. No UH-60L mod or external scripts need installation by players.

NAVIGATION / INTELLIGENCE
WP1 FOOTHOLD. WP2 IP / transport hold. WP3 PLANNED LZ. WP4 HOME (FOOTHOLD). Enemy sites are TARGET POINTS ONLY, not flight-route waypoints.
MMS TARGET POINTS: 1T = STRELA-10 (SA13); 2T = HOSTAGE BUILDING (UNK, NO FIRE). These are separate Navigation Target Fix Points in the aircraft target database. To slew the MMS, select PREPT on its Mode Selector, use Manual/Slave as needed until the advisory reads PREPT, press R2 PPT, enter 1T or 2T on the multifunction keyboard and press Enter. Target-point loading and sensor alignment need cockpit verification; neither point is an automatic lock or authorization to fire. TIS/TV selection is independent.
Choose a terrain-masked approach. The building is a protected no-fire location. The exact hostage building and Strela are marked on F10 and stored as 1T/2T; all coordinates identify mission objects in DCS planar metres: building x=64200, east=20150; Strela x=63600, east=18100. F10 places them geographically and mission-start messages provide lat/lon when available.
FOOTHOLD is now the departure and final recovery FARP, 15 nm from the village, with fixed pads that are never moved under starting aircraft. KEYSTONE remains an alternate service base about 25 nm from the village and 10 nm behind FOOTHOLD. Its complete camp footprint is checked for land, slope and scenery during initialization; it can shift by up to 1 nm to find an open site. Use the actual F10 KEYSTONE marker. KEYSTONE radio: 128.500 AM. Both bases offer spaced visible helipads, fuel, ammunition, ground crew and repairs with unlimited pad resources. Landing at KEYSTONE does not complete the rescue: escort Lifeline back to FOOTHOLD.
Departure to objective: 15.0 nm, about 10 minutes at 90 knots. Return is the same distance: approximately 30 nm round trip before combat, holding and three minutes on the ground. Allow roughly 30-45 minutes overall. The village is an authored mission compound; terrain/scenery appearance still needs flight verification.

EXECUTION
Clear the Strela and the guards around the compound/LZ, positively identifying targets before firing. Hostages can die from fire, explosions or destruction of their building. Continue rescuing survivors after casualties. Lifeline will never enter merely because defenders are killed: use F10 > Other > Transport > Clear Black Hawk to land. Clearance is rejected while the known Strela or close defenders still threaten the site. The actual LZ is terrain/scenery-checked near WP3; the F10 LZ marker and requested green smoke identify it.
Once Lifeline is landed within 80 m of the LZ and below 1 m/s, the simulated team needs 180 seconds to secure the survivors and board. Cover it. A local threat, movement or wave-off resets rescue progress; re-clear once safe. Ground-team movement and boarding are represented by timing/messages, not passenger animation. Neutral infantry models stand in for hostages and do not fight.
Enemy reinforcements begin moving about three minutes after your flight enters 8 km of the compound. Defeating every enemy is optional. Keep the approaches clear while Lifeline is on the ground.
After boarding Lifeline returns to its own pad at FOOTHOLD. Escort it home. It must land there for 20 seconds to count the rescued hostages: six is full success; one to five is partial success. No survivors, Black Hawk loss or player helicopter loss is failure. Flying continues after the result.

F10 / RADIOS
OPEN DOOR > Transport: clearance; hold / wave off; abort and return. OPEN DOOR > Rescue: status; mark actual LZ green.
Wave-off returns Lifeline to its hold and resets the rescue timer; it needs fresh clearance. Abort before boarding cancels the extraction and returns empty (mission failure once home). After boarding, abort/wave-off returns home with those aboard. Do not fire on the marked hostage building.
UHF package 251.000 AM. FOOTHOLD 129.500 AM; transport pad 129.000 AM. KEYSTONE alternate 128.500 AM. Ground servicing still needs DCS confirmation.

PROGRESS REPORTS
Lifeline reports final approach, rescue start/halfway, interruptions, actual airborne return with survivor count and recovery approach. Reports appear as text; no recorded voice audio. Sentinel describes targets relative to the hostage building using approximate grid directions before giving coordinates and Kiowa-relative bearing/range.

DRONE LASER SUPPORT
Sentinel is an unarmed MQ-9 staged 15 nm from the objective at 20,000 ft MSL (6096 m). It automatically transits to orbit above the village at mission start and reports when on station. Initial on-station entry requires being within 2.5 km and 500 m of assigned altitude. After arrival, the orbit envelope extends to 4 km and 750 m altitude difference to prevent boundary interruptions. Arrival is announced only once. At 70 m/s, allow roughly seven minutes for transit; arrival depends on native AI flight. The high orbit reduces exposure to short-range defenses, but does not guarantee concealment or survival. F10 > Other > Drone commands: Designate next target, Laser status, Stop lasing. Laser status reports a lost/unavailable drone explicitly. Target reports provide decimal-degree latitude/longitude plus true bearing/range in nautical miles from your Kiowa (explicit grid-bearing fallback when geographic conversion is unavailable). Drone API faults disable optional support while the rescue continues. Match your Hellfire seeker to laser code 1688; use the Kiowa's appropriate remote-laser engagement procedure and positively identify the target before firing. No automatic weapons release or extraction clearance. Requests cycle through eligible hostile ground units, prioritizing the known SAM. Lasing requires terrain line of sight and a 15 km slant range; buildings/vegetation can still obstruct the beam. Targets within 100 m of the hostage building/survivors or 300 m of friendly helicopters are excluded. Moving or masked targets can lose designation; request again. These buffers do not guarantee safe weapon effects. Drone loss does not fail the rescue. Native orbit, laser visibility and remote Hellfire acquisition require flight verification.

BUILD STATUS
Development build. Automated checks do not certify native UH-60A follow, temporary landing, takeoff/recovery, terrain placement or actual combat. Requires an in-simulator sortie. Requires Syria and OH-58D only.
